'Glimvers' is a subproperty of 'ostrels'.why: "Glimvers" and "ostrels" are made-up relations (catalogued as glimvers and ostrels, fictional): neither is a word anyone uses, so a model has no default reading of one as a special case of the other. The instances are real predator and prey pairs that nobody has recorded under these names.

Voles are rodents..why: The first sentence of the vole article.

sources.quote: Voles are small rodents that are relatives of lemmings and hamsters, but with a stouter body; a longer, hairy tail; a slightly rounder head; smaller eyes and ears; and differently formed molars.

Voles are birds..why: Deliberately false so the disjunction turns on the inserted property: voles are small rodents.

notes: RBox expansion paired with biology-replace-0010 ('is a lobe of' stops being a subproperty of 'is part of'): gives a made-up relation (glimvers, a subproperty of the equally made-up ostrels) the property the revision changes, applied to real instances in the prompt. Instances are predator-prey pairs (barn owl and vole, red fox and European rabbit); the direct and first instance are yes, the second ('could fail') is no. The coined terms stay untranslated in the Chinese and Spanish prompts. hops counts the prompt facts as one bridge. Unrelated near and far ask other properties of real relations that the edit must not change. Locality references are the logical answers; scoring uses each model's own pre-edit answer.
